claims.claim: This is a Used Nikon D3400 DSLR Camera With 70-300mm Lens.
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a black Nikon DSLR with a large zoom lens and a DX label on the lens barrel, but the exact camera model (D3400) and the exact lens model/part number (70-300mm) are not readable from the provided angles.

claims.claim: Working perfectly ok with no fault.
claims.evidence: No proof of operation is shown (no shutter test, autofocus test, screen/EVF check, or sensor/lens clarity inspection).
Witness report states Nikon logo is visible on the camera body in Photo 0 and Photo 1.

risks.risk: Wrong camera model or wrong lens specification (e.g., not actually D3400 and/or not actually 70-300mm). This affects compatibility and resale value.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the camera model text on the body (e.g., 'D3400') and a clear close-up of the lens model/part number and focal length markings (e.g., '70-300mm') on the lens barrel.
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unspecified Nikon DX DSLR with an unspecified telephoto zoom lens (worst-case for model/lens certainty).

risks.risk: Non-working or degraded performance (shutter issues, autofocus failure, dead pixels, sensor dust, or lens haze/fungus).
risks.proof: Video/clip showing: power-on with live view, autofocus lock on a high-contrast object, and a short shutter test (multiple shots) plus a photo of a blank white wall at f/8 to reveal sensor dust.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not fully tested / potentially faulty (worst-case).

risks.risk: Physical condition issues (scuffs/damage near edges; possible screen/eyepiece scratches not shown).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of: LCD screen, viewfinder/eyepiece, lens front element, and all edges/corners under light.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used with cosmetic wear (worst-case within what’s visible).

risks.risk: Missing accessories (battery, charger, memory card, lens hood, straps, manuals). Missing items reduce usability and value.
risks.proof: A full photo spread laid out showing every included accessory, with labels/part numbers where applicable.

risks.risk: Battery health/charge holding capacity unknown; may require replacement.
risks.proof: A clip showing battery level after a short test (power-on + live view + autofocus + taking a few shots) and/or a battery health indicator if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming battery may be weak (worst-case).

risks.risk: Potential scam/misrepresentation risk due to brand conflict (seller says Canon, witness photos show Nikon).
risks.proof: Photo of the camera body showing the brand/model clearly (Nikon logo and model) plus lens markings; also confirm the exact items included.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest tier for uncertainty and treat as high risk until verified.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the camera model text on the body (confirm D3400 or exact model).
Clear close-up photo of the lens barrel markings showing the exact lens model and focal length (confirm 70-300mm).
Power-on video showing live view, LCD/EVF clarity, and autofocus working on a target.
Short shutter test clip (take a few shots) and a sample image showing sensor dust (white wall shot).
Close-up photos of LCD screen, viewfinder/eyepiece, lens front element, and all edges/corners under light.
Photo of all included accessories laid out (battery, charger, memory card, lens hood, straps, manuals/box if any).
Battery test clip showing it holds charge during the short shooting sequence.
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a Nikon DSLR with a telephoto zoom, but the exact D3400 model and 70-300mm lens cannot be verified from the photos, and the 'working perfectly' claim has no operational proof. Also, the seller’s 'Canon' statement conflicts with the Nikon logo seen, increasing misrepresentation risk.
